journey: Arrived, read welcome card (likes '1 to 24 guests')

gave_up_at: Double feature shopping list still says serves 4 for a youth group of 20

frictions.what: Double feature and marathon menus ignore Usual guests. Set to 20, the double feature still says 'serves 4' and its shopping list says 'Serves 4' with no guest stepper
frictions.where: Double feature dialog and its Shopping list; Plan a marathon

frictions.what: Scaling to 20 to 24 is arithmetic only. Spoon measures balloon ('24 tbsp sprinkles', '30 tbsp chocolate syrup', '20 tbsp plain flour', '10 cup ice'), plurals break ('5 small bunch mints', '5 handful mint leaves'), and odd precision ('1.13kg plain flour'). Method text is not scaled: Home Alone at 24 still says 'fill four tall glasses' and 'six scoops of ice cream', 'tip into a baking dish' for 2.4kg macaroni
frictions.where: Prep sheet at 20 and 24 guests (Home Alone, Jurassic Park, Moana)

frictions.what: Double feature for a church youth group spun Arthur and Pretty Woman with champagne, Kir royale, brandy and bitters. Nothing suggests turning on No alcohol or picking a crowd-friendly pair
Guest cap of 24 is fine for 20, but church nights often run 30 plus and there is no way past 24
'Longest dish 4 hr 5 min' on Home Alone is just chilling cola overnight, which makes a simple menu look like a big job

wishes: Guest stepper on double feature and marathon lists
Crowd mode: trays, batch sizes, 'buy 3 x 1kg packs' instead of 2.4kg
Allow more than 24 guests
Youth-group friendly pairs (PG, no alcohol)
loved: The cinema front and spin wheel, the kids will love it on the TV
Shopping list grouped by aisle
Marathon plan for Toy Story 1 to 4 with one combined menu
quote: Mate, it's beautiful and the youth will love the wheel, but when I set 20 people and the double feature still says serves 4, I'm back doing maths on the back of the church bulletin.
would_pay: maybe, a few dollars a year if crowd sizes actually flow through everything

gave_up_at: No nut filter or warnings; E.T. menu is peanut butter end to end

frictions.what: No allergen flags and no nut-free filter. By my scan 131 of the 328 kids-mode films have nuts somewhere in their recipes. E.T. (rated PG, served up in kids mode) is built around peanut butter: 350g peanut butter, peanut butter candy trail, homemade peanut butter cups, with no warning. Home Alone's sundae bar has 480g roasted peanuts. Candy bar sells rocky road with peanuts and chocolate-coated peanuts with no allergy marker
frictions.where: Prep sheet, recipes, Candy bar, Goes well with
frictions.evidence: E.T. prep sheet text; Home Alone prep text; /tmp/claude-0/-home-claude/6a0d96ab-f9fb-5c75-b6b0-4681bb3c85ff/scratchpad/fg/shots/P22-09-candybar.png

frictions.what: Kids mode uses G or PG ratings, so it lets through The Fifth Element, Batman Forever, Gremlins, Rear Window and Pretty in Pink. Fine for 10 year olds, not for under 8s. Find a film ignores kids mode completely (Cinderella Man, a boxing film, shows up as a match). The programme dropdown still says 'Everything (850 films)' and theme counts are for all films
frictions.where: Wheel in kids mode, Find a film search, Tonight's programme dropdown

frictions.what: Settings only has Vegetarian and No alcohol. No allergens at all (nuts, gluten, dairy, egg, sesame)
'Goes well with' suggests Rocky road (with peanuts) next to Home Alone, a film already carrying a peanut sundae bar

wishes: Nut-free toggle that swaps or hides dishes and snacks
Allergen tags on every dish and candy bar item (peanut, tree nut, sesame, egg, dairy, gluten)
'May contain' note on Buy it items
Age filter: under 5, under 8, under 12
loved: Kids mode forcing alcohol-free drinks automatically
Spin animation and the ticket stubs
Shopping list checkboxes that survive a reload
quote: It's gorgeous, but the first family film I opened was E.T. and it's peanut butter three ways with no warning. I can't hand this to my husband to cook from.
would_pay: maybe, if allergens were properly flagged, I'd pay for that peace of mind
